title: [Misc] Add numpy implementation of `compute_slot_mapping`

experiments.name: compute_slot_mapping
experiments.workload: Prefill slot-mapping build in vllm/attention/backends/utils.py: fill the per-token slot_mapping list from a block_table over a large token range (numel >= 256, the author's large-list regime).
experiments.note: Diff adds _compute_slot_mapping_numpy (vectorized np.arange / block_table[idx]) alongside the original per-token python loop, dispatching to numpy only when numel >= _COMPUTE_SLOT_MAPPING_NUMPY_NUMEL (256) to avoid numpy-array setup overhead on small lists. Number is the author's body claim 'up to 3x speedup with large lists'; no absolute timings published.

reported.scope: author's 'up to 3x' is a speedup ceiling for the large-list regime only, with no absolute baseline and no fixed list length given
reported.scale_short: Author gave only a ratio (up to 3x) for unspecified 'large' lists, no absolute us/ms and no list size. TO MAKE 1:1: microbench _compute_slot_mapping_numpy vs _compute_slot_mapping_python at a fixed numel (e.g. 4096) and report the measured ratio in the same regime.
reported.scale_note: This is a pure CPU list-building helper, so it is reproducible off-GPU, but the author published only a qualitative '3x' upper bound. pct is stored as 2.0 (3x = +200%) per the ratio shape; the author baseline renders as none and the solution is reconstructed from our measured baseline. Gain shrinks toward 1x as numel approaches the 256 switch threshold and the python path is slower only above it.

environment: reported-only: author's published numbers; measured arms pending on GPU box
